notes:
The Marilyn Blaisdell Photograph Collection read whole — 483 catalogue records. Blaisdell was a collector and dealer, not a photographer, so the collection is an assembled miscellany of historical San Francisco views bought in from many studios, and the description sentence names no maker.

459 of the 483 records give no street number and are skipped per `COLLECTION_UNNUMBERED_POLICY`: bay views, parades, cable cars, the Cliff House, the 1906 fire seen from a hill. 13 findings came out of the rest.

**Eight candidates were the collection's own plate numbers** and are now guarded against. Blaisdell's stereographs are titled with their serial at the head — "877 A view of San Francisco Bay looking south from Yerba Buena Island", "3022 Ferry-boat entering Oakland slip", "1704 Mission Church, Mission Dolores", "320. Visit of French Admiral Cloue and staff" — and all fourteen title-initial numbers in the collection are plate numbers while every genuine address is mid-caption. `COLLECTION_PLATE_NUMBERS` strips a title-initial number for this collection alone; 779 titles corpus-wide open with a real street number, so it cannot be a general rule. A ninth was a clock time: "at 1:00 P. M." yielded *00 P. M*, now refused by the colon before the number.

**12 of the 13 findings are unresolved, and almost all of them for the right reason.** The collection's addressed half is 1880s–1914, so `resolve_eas.py` refuses anything dated before 1910 on the 1909 renumbering rule — 412 Sacramento Street (1899), 25 Geary Street (1904), 810 Montgomery (1906), 1613 Stockton Street (1908), 320 Market Street (c. 1907–08), 690 Market Street (c. 1889–94), 1822 Eddy Street (1906), 19 Oak Street (1906) and three plates of 747 Baker Street in the weeks after the fire. Several of those match EAS cleanly, which is exactly what makes them dangerous. The one resolution is 101 Waverly Place, 1914, past the cutoff.

**Privacy: this collection files its people in `700$a`, not `600$a`, and the redactor could not see them.** Seven plates of 747 Baker Street name the household that photographed its own house after the earthquake, catalogued as `700 $e Photographer`. A name written into a caption is a person in the frame whatever the record credits them for elsewhere, and "…home at 747 Baker Street" is a sentence about who lived at a street number. `redact()` now reads both fields; the guard against taking a building or a street with them is that a bare surname is left alone when the next word says it is a place ("Canterbury Hotel", "747 Baker Street").

One record loses a fact the extractor cannot take: "L. Lerda Wine Cellar at 814 and European Hotel at 810 Montgomery between Jackson and Pacific Streets" gives two businesses at two numbers, and only 810 is recorded. Neither number is in EAS today, so nothing was published either way.

coverage.note: Read every record in the collection: 483 unique catalogue records, 24 of which parse a street number in the title. Eight of those are the collection's own plate numbers and one a clock time, all now refused at extraction; 13 findings remain over 13 distinct addresses. 1 resolved and published; 12 unresolved, of which 11 are refused by the pre-1910 renumbering rule and 1 is a condominium today.

publish.note: Timeline entry. The page is the parcel's, filed at 818 Clay Street; the photograph is of 101 Waverly Place, which EAS puts on the same parcel, so the description keeps the number the plate was made at. The 2025 roll dates the building 1907, seven years before the photograph, so the building described is the one standing.

citation.label: 690 Market Street, circa 1889 to 1894. Marilyn Blaisdell Photograph Collection (SFP 84), San Francisco History Center, San Francisco Public Library.

resolution.method: sf-eas-addresses has 690 MARKET ST but it does not join to one parcel. 690 MARKET ST's coordinates fall in 20 active parcels (0311078, 0311105, 0311049, 0311059…), which is what a condominium looks like in sf-parcels: one parcel per unit, none of them the building.
resolution.note: The address is a condominium today, and the directory contract in the root AGENTS.md defers those: each unit has its own parcel and none of them is the building the record names.
